name.text: Solve simultaneous equations graphically (cubic and line)

questiontext.text:
Solve the following simultaneous equations graphically, for \( {@xlo@} \le x \le {@xhi@} \).

\[ {#eq1tex#} \qquad \text{and} \qquad {#eq2tex#} \]

(a) Plot the graphs of equations above on the grid by dragging the red points to draw the curve and blue points for the straight line.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="refQ1" input-ref-ans2="refQ2" input-ref-ans3="refP1" input-ref-ans4="refP2" width="640px" height="560px"]] var xlo = {#xlo#}, xhi = {#xhi#}, ymin = {#ymin#}, ymax = {#ymax#}; /* keepaspectratio: true gives the SAME scale on both axes (square grid cells) */ var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [xlo - 1.5, ymax + 1.5, xhi + 1.5, ymin - 1.5], axis: false, grid: false, keepaspectratio: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false} }); /* the visible area after the 1:1 adjustment: [left, top, right, bottom] */ var bb = board.getBoundingBox(); var u = board.unitX; /* pixels per unit (identical for x and y) */ var left = Math.ceil(bb[0]), right = Math.floor(bb[2]), top = Math.floor(bb[1]), bottom = Math.ceil(bb[3]); var step = Math.ceil(28 / u); /* number every "step" units, so neighbouring labels are always at least 28 px apart */ var gi; /* square grid: one line for every whole number across the whole visible board */ for (gi = left; gi != right + 1; gi++) { board.create('segment', [ [gi, bb[3]], [gi, bb[1]] ], {strokeColor: '#d4d4d4', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false, layer: 0}); } for (gi = bottom; gi != top + 1; gi++) { board.create('segment', [ [bb[0], gi], [bb[2], gi] ], {strokeColor: '#d4d4d4', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false, layer: 0}); } /* axes with arrow heads */ board.create('arrow', [ [bb[0], 0], [bb[2], 0] ], {strokeColor: '#222222', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false, layer: 2}); board.create('arrow', [ [0, bb[3]], [0, bb[1]] ], {strokeColor: '#222222', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false, layer: 2}); /* tick marks and numbers, drawn one by one: x numbers are centred directly under their grid line; y numbers sit to the LEFT of the y-axis, level with their grid line */ for (gi = left; gi != right + 1; gi++) { if (gi !== 0) { board.create('segment', [ [gi, -4 / u], [gi, 4 / u] ], {strokeColor: '#222222', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false, layer: 2}); if (gi % step === 0) { board.create('text', [gi, -9 / u, '' + gi], {fixed: true, highlight: false, anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 13}); } } } for (gi = bottom; gi != top + 1; gi++) { if (gi !== 0) { board.create('segment', [ [-4 / u, gi], [4 / u, gi] ], {strokeColor: '#222222', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false, layer: 2}); if (gi % step === 0) { board.create('text', [-9 / u, gi, '' + gi], {fixed: true, highlight: false, anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'middle', fontSize: 13}); } } } board.create('text', [-9 / u, -9 / u, '0'], {fixed: true, highlight: false, anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 13}); board.create('text', [bb[2] - 6 / u, 12 / u, 'x'], {fixed: true, highlight: false, anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'bottom', fontSize: 16}); board.create('text', [10 / u, bb[1] - 6 / u, 'y'], {fixed: true, highlight: false, anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 16}); /* four free handles, snapped to the grid; none of the start positions is a correct answer */ var snapAttr = {name: '', size: 6, snapToGrid: true, snapSizeX: 1, snapSizeY: 1, showInfobox: true}; var Q1 = board.create('point', [xlo + 1, 0], JXG.merge(snapAttr, {strokeColor: '#c62828', fillColor: '#c62828'})); var Q2 = board.create('point', [xlo + 2, 0], JXG.merge(snapAttr, {strokeColor: '#c62828', fillColor: '#c62828'})); var P1 = board.create('point', [0, -1], JXG.merge(snapAttr, {strokeColor: '#1565c0', fillColor: '#1565c0'})); var P2 = board.create('point', [2, -1], JXG.merge(snapAttr, {strokeColor: '#1565c0', fillColor: '#1565c0'})); /* the curve y = x^3 - B x^2 + C through the two red points (B and C solved from the points) */ function cubicPars() { var u1 = Q1.X(), v1 = Q1.Y(), u2 = Q2.X(), v2 = Q2.Y(), dd = u1 * u1 - u2 * u2; if (dd === 0) { return null; } var B = ((v2 - u2 * u2 * u2) - (v1 - u1 * u1 * u1)) / dd; return [B, (v1 - u1 * u1 * u1) + B * u1 * u1]; } var curve = board.create('functiongraph', [function(t) { var p = cubicPars(); return (p === null) ? NaN : t * t * t - p[0] * t * t + p[1]; }, xlo, xhi], {strokeColor: '#c62828', strokeWidth: 3}); var line = board.create('line', [P1, P2], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 3}); stack_jxg.bind_point(refQ1, Q1); stack_jxg.bind_point(refQ2, Q2); stack_jxg.bind_point(refP1, P1); stack_jxg.bind_point(refP2, P2); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) Plotting the graphs.

Make a table of values for the curve \( {#eq1tex#} \) (two points are enough for the board, the rest help you sketch it):

\[ \begin{array}{c|cccccc} x & -2 & -1 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline y & {@cvals[1]@} & {@cvals[2]@} & {@cvals[3]@} & {@cvals[4]@} & {@cvals[5]@} & {@cvals[6]@} \end{array} \]

and for the straight line \( {#eq2tex#} \):

\[ \begin{array}{c|cccccc} x & -2 & -1 & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline y & {@lvals[1]@} & {@lvals[2]@} & {@lvals[3]@} & {@lvals[4]@} & {@lvals[5]@} & {@lvals[6]@} \end{array} \] [[jsxgraph width="640px" height="560px"]] var xlo = {#xlo#}, xhi = {#xhi#}, ymin = {#ymin#}, ymax = {#ymax#}; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [xlo - 0.8, ymax + 1.2, xhi + 0.8, ymin - 1.2], axis: false, grid: false, keepaspectratio: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false} }); /* labelled square grid, one line per whole number */ var gi; for (gi = xlo - 1; gi != xhi + 2; gi++) { board.create('line', [ [gi, 0], [gi, 1] ], {strokeColor: '#d4d4d4', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false, layer: 0}); } for (gi = ymin - 2; gi != ymax + 3; gi++) { board.create('line', [ [0, gi], [1, gi] ], {strokeColor: '#d4d4d4', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false, layer: 0}); } board.create('axis', [ [0,0], [1,0] ], {strokeColor: '#222222', strokeWidth: 2, ticks: {ticksDistance: 1, insertTicks: false, minorTicks: 0, majorHeight: 10}}); board.create('axis', [ [0,0], [0,1] ], {strokeColor: '#222222', strokeWidth: 2, ticks: {ticksDistance: 1, insertTicks: false, minorTicks: 0, majorHeight: 10}}); board.create('text', [xhi + 0.7, 0.5, 'x'], {fixed: true, anchorX: 'right', fontSize: 16}); board.create('text', [0.3, ymax + 1.1, 'y'], {fixed: true, anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 16}); board.create('text', [-0.12, -0.1, '0'], {fixed: true, anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'top', fontSize: 12}); var bb = {#bb#}, cc = {#cc#}; var curve = board.create('functiongraph', [function(t) { return t * t * t - bb * t * t + cc; }, xlo, xhi], {strokeColor: '#c62828', strokeWidth: 3, fixed: true}); var L1 = board.create('point', [0, bb], {visible: false, withLabel: false, name: ''}); var L2 = board.create('point', [1, 1 + bb], {visible: false, withLabel: false, name: ''}); var line = board.create('line', [L1, L2], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 3, fixed: true}); /* label placement: try 24 directions, keep the one furthest (in screen pixels) from the curve, the line, the axes and the board edges */ function labelAttr(px, py) { var ux = board.unitX, uy = board.unitY, R = 44; function clear(x, y) { var fx = x * x * x - bb * x * x + cc, slope = 3 * x * x - 2 * bb * x; var dCurve = Math.abs(y - fx) * uy / Math.sqrt(1 + Math.pow(slope * uy / ux, 2)); var dLine = Math.abs(y - x - bb) * uy / Math.sqrt(1 + Math.pow(uy / ux, 2)); return Math.min(dCurve, dLine, Math.abs(x) * ux, Math.abs(y) * uy, (x - (xlo - 0.8)) * ux, (xhi + 0.8 - x) * ux, (ymax + 1.2 - y) * uy, (y - (ymin - 1.2)) * uy); } var cands = [], k; for (k = 0; k != 24; k++) { cands.push(k * Math.PI / 12); } var score = cands.map(function(t) { var cx = px + R * Math.cos(t) / ux, cy = py + R * Math.sin(t) / uy; return Math.min(clear(cx, cy), clear(cx - 36 / ux, cy), clear(cx + 36 / ux, cy)); }); var t = cands[score.indexOf(Math.max.apply(null, score))]; return {offset: [Math.round(R * Math.cos(t)), Math.round(R * Math.sin(t))], anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'middle'}; } var sols = [ [{#sx1#}, {#sy1#}], [{#sx2#}, {#sy2#}], [{#sx3#}, {#sy3#}] ]; sols.forEach(function(sp) { board.create('segment', [ [sp[0], sp[1]], [sp[0], 0] ], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#777777', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}); board.create('segment', [ [sp[0], sp[1]], [0, sp[1]] ], {dash: 2, strokeColor: '#777777', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}); var lab = labelAttr(sp[0], sp[1]); lab.fontSize = 15; board.create('point', sp, {name: '(' + sp[0] + ', ' + sp[1] + ')', size: 5, strokeColor: '#2e7d32', fillColor: '#2e7d32', fixed: true, label: lab}); }); [[/jsxgraph]]

(b) Reading the solutions from the graph. The line and the curve cross at the three green points. The dashed guides show their coordinates:

\[ [{@sx1@},\ {@sy1@}], \qquad [{@sx2@},\ {@sy2@}], \qquad [{@sx3@},\ {@sy3@}]. \]

Why these are solutions. A solution of simultaneous equations must make both equations true at the same time. Substitute each point back into the two equations.

For \( x={@sx1@},\ y={@sy1@} \):

\[ \begin{align*} \text{Curve: } x^3-(b)x^2+(c) &= ({@sx1@})^3-({@bb@})({@sx1@})^2+({@cc@}) = {@sy1@} = y \; \checkmark \\ \text{Line: } x+(b) &= ({@sx1@})+({@bb@}) = {@sy1@} = y \; \checkmark \end{align*} \]

For \( x={@sx2@},\ y={@sy2@} \):

\[ \begin{align*} \text{Curve: } x^3-(b)x^2+(c) &= ({@sx2@})^3-({@bb@})({@sx2@})^2+({@cc@}) = {@sy2@} = y \; \checkmark \\ \text{Line: } x+(b) &= ({@sx2@})+({@bb@}) = {@sy2@} = y \; \checkmark \end{align*} \]

For \( x={@sx3@},\ y={@sy3@} \):

\[ \begin{align*} \text{Curve: } x^3-(b)x^2+(c) &= ({@sx3@})^3-({@bb@})({@sx3@})^2+({@cc@}) = {@sy3@} = y \; \checkmark \\ \text{Line: } x+(b) &= ({@sx3@})+({@bb@}) = {@sy3@} = y \; \checkmark \end{align*} \]

Each point gives the same value of \( y \) in both equations, so the line and the curve really do meet there.

falsefeedback.text: Your two red points do not fix a curve of this kind: their \( x \)-values are the same or opposites. Choose two points on the curve whose \( x \)-values are not opposites of each other.

node.description: both red points lie on the curve

truefeedback.text: Your curve crosses the y-axis at the right place, but its shape is not right. Check the \( x^2 \) term: use a table of values and take care with the sign of \( b \).
The shape of your curve is close, but it is not at the right height. Where should the curve \( {#eq1tex#} \) cross the y-axis (put \( x=0 \))?

falsefeedback.text: Your red points are not both on the curve \( {#eq1tex#} \). Make a table of values: choose an \( x \), work out \( y \), and place a red point there.
Your two blue points are on top of each other. Place them at different positions so that they define a straight line.

node.description: both blue points lie on y = x + b

truefeedback.text: The steepness of your line is right, but it does not cut the y-axis in the right place. Compare the constant term in \( {#eq2tex#} \) with where your line crosses the y-axis.
Your line crosses the y-axis in the right place, but its steepness is wrong. For \( y=x+b \), how far up does the line go for each 1 step to the right?

falsefeedback.text: Your line is not the graph of \( {#eq2tex#} \). Make a table of values: choose two values of \( x \), work out \( y \) for each, and place the blue points there.

truefeedback.text: Two of your points are solutions, but the third is not (or you repeated a point). A cubic curve and a line can cross up to three times: look again at the whole interval.
Only one of your points is a solution. The line and the curve cross three times in this interval; read the coordinates of each crossing from the grid, and enter three different points.
None of your points is where the line and the curve cross. A solution lies on both graphs: read its \( x \) and \( y \) values from the grid.

falsefeedback.text: Careful with the order: write each solution as \( [x, y] \), with the \( x \)-value (across) first and the \( y \)-value (up) second.
